issue.title: Add labels for screen readers to the upload inputs and buttons
issue.body:
The UI has no `aria-*` attributes or `<label>` elements at all. The kernel and initramfs file pickers only have a styled `<div>` above them, so a screen reader announces them as just "file". The hex text box only has a placeholder. And the emoji icons inside buttons get read out loud ("television Noise").

**Where:** `src/main.ts`, the HTML template from about line 48 to line 186. The main spots are the hex textarea (~147), `kernel-input` (~159), `initrd-input` (~162), and the `btn-icon` spans in every button.

**Done when:**
- The textarea and the two visible file inputs each have a real label (`<label for>` or `aria-label`)
- The emoji spans are hidden from screen readers
- The page looks the same as before
- `npm run build` passes

**Hint:** turning the existing caption `<div>`s into `<label>`s gives you the labels without changing the layout. Check your work with your browser's accessibility inspector.

explanation.summary: Add accessible names to the hex text area and the kernel and initramfs file inputs so screen readers can identify them. Hide decorative emoji inside buttons from screen readers while keeping the page looking the same.
explanation.why_it_matters: This helps people who use screen readers understand and use the upload controls and buttons.

files.why: These buttons contain emoji in `btn-icon` spans, which the issue says should not be read aloud.
These buttons also contain emoji in `btn-icon` spans that should be hidden from screen readers.

concepts.explanation: A `<label>` with a `for` value matching a control's ID gives that control a name that assistive technology can announce.
The `aria-label` attribute provides an accessible name for a control without displaying extra text.
The `aria-hidden` attribute can keep decorative content, such as an emoji, out of what screen readers announce.

done_when: The textarea and the two visible file inputs each have a real label (`<label for>` or `aria-label`).
The emoji spans are hidden from screen readers.
The page looks the same as before.
explanation.unsure_about: Heads up: I couldn't see the textarea, file inputs, or all the `btn-icon` spans. Open `src/main.ts` around lines 147–186 and search for `kernel-input`, `initrd-input`, and `btn-icon` before you start.
